newsitem.title: USA: Florida insurance pool to cut size in half by Feb.
newsitem.headline: Florida insurance pool to cut size in half by Feb.

text.p: The Florida Residential Property and Casualty joint underwriting association (JUA) said it plans to place roughly half its policies with private insurers by mid-February in an accelerated effort to reduce its size.
As of September, there were more than 936,000 residential policies in the JUA. The goal is to place more than 450,000 policies with private insurers by February 15, 1997, the JUA said.
Under state law, policyholders who are offered coverage by an approved private insurer are no longer eligible for coverage by the JUA, the JUA said.
Cutting the number of policies in the JUA is a top priority of State Treasurer and Insurance Commissioner Bill Nelson, the JUA Board of Governors and the Legislature, the JUA said.

Placing policyholders currently in the JUA with private insurers is considered key to restoring the health of Florida's property insurance market, which was severely impacted by Hurricane Andrew in 1992, the JUA said.
The JUA said it will transfer policyholders to the insurance companies through three methods: non-renewals, 30-day cancellations and policy assumptions.

Under state law in effect in 1995 and mid-1996, the principal method of placing homeowners with a private insurer was for the JUA to issue a notice of non-renewal at least 90 days prior to the normal expiration date of the policy tagged for removal, the JUA said.
It said this method will continue to be used, whenever possible.
The JUA said it also can transfer policyholders through 30-day cancellations.

In the 1996 legislative session, state lawmakers approved a measure authorizing the JUA to issue 30-day cancellation notices in instances where policyholders are no longer eligible for coverage because a private insurer has agreed to offer coverage to them.
In these instances, the JUA said it will issue cancellation notices 40 days prior to the effective cancellation date of the policy.
Within three days of receiving these notices, policyholders also will receive an offer of coverage from the new insurer, the JUA said.

Checks for the unused portion of the premium originally paid to the JUA will be mailed, along with the cancellation notice, to the policyholder, mortgage company or premium finance company, depending on which party is responsible for making the next property insurance payment, the JUA said.
The JUA said it also is working with some insurance companies on plans in which they will remove JUA policies using assumptions.

In this instance, the insurer assumes responsibility for all of the JUA's obligations, including all responsibility for losses occurring on or after the assumption date, the JUA said. These policies will not be canceled at that time, but will remain in effect until their normal expiration date.
The policyholders, mortgage companies and insurance agents will all receive notices that the policies are being assumed.
Unearned premium checks will not be returned under this method because the policies will remain in effect, with the same coverages and rates, the JUA said.

Under each of these three transfer methods, policyholders have the option of shopping for private coverage on their own if they do not want to accept the offer from the private insurer which tagged their policy, the JUA said.
But they are no longer eligible for coverage in the JUA.
People who have mortgages on their homes generally must either accept the policy offered to them or find a policy from another insurance company to meet mortgage requirements.
Otherwise, the mortgage company may put a policy into effect that may be more expensive and may provide less coverage than other policies available to them, the JUA said.
The JUA said it is setting up a toll free telephone number in mid-November to assist policyholders who have questions about the 30-day cancellations.
The number will be included on their cancellation notices.
